e.note: Best: A3 at 19.2% reach vs 6.3% for the benchmark

e.text: A3 leads at 19.2%, triple the 6.3% benchmark; asking the Critic how to push it further.

e.note: Reading results for A3, A1, A2

critique.summary: A3 leads on every measure (19.2% reach, 10th percentile 17.1%, $624 per point, about 3x the benchmark's $1894) because early podcasts and the Nasty Gal drop give word of mouth time to work (58.6% of adoption), and even its 10th percentile beats A1's and A2's means. Late pop-ups (day 38), Little Village social ads and the Douglas and Near West Side partners return little for their cost, and McKinley Park (zone 2, fit 0.713) is barely seeded by A3.

findings.finding: The Nasty Gal drop (10.9% of adoption for $2000) and host-read ads on Insanely Chill (8.0%, $3400) and Very Really Good (6.4%, $3400) carry the plan, and it reaches 19.2% (17.1%–21.4%) at $624 per point.
Lower West Side social ads earn only 2.6% for $2280, about the same as single $300 partners like Vault Gallerie (2.3%), and the Podcasts and sitcom reruns district lags at 11.2%.

The Elite Daily drop (11.7%, $2000) and the $300 Lower West Side partners work, but the day-38 Plaza Garibaldi party (1.4%, $2500) and Little Village social ads (1.6%, $2400) are too late or too weak, leaving 14.6% reach at $793 per point.

Citywide social ads earn 15.6% for $4320, but the Douglas and Near West Side partners (Sage Room, Midwest Coast, Succezz) earn just 0.8% each in zones that hold only 2.4–2.5% of the audience, and the 10th percentile of 12.1% is the weakest of the three.
Spending by population alone gets 6.3% at $1894 per point, and its street teams earn only 0.5–0.9% each for $450.

changes.change: Keep A3's podcasts on days 3 and 10 and the Nasty Gal drop, and add the Elite Daily drop (11.7% in A1) by cutting social:0 Lower West Side ads to about 15 days.
changes.why: Co-branded drops return roughly 5–6% of adoption per $1000, against about 1.1% per $1000 for local social ads.

changes.change: Add McKinley Park and Little Village partners such as One City Tap and Mi Tierra ($300 each, 2.1% each in A2) to A3.
changes.why: Zone 2 (fit 0.713) is unseeded, and $300 partners return about 2% each, far above any ad or party per dollar.

changes.change: Drop all day-38 pop-ups, social:3 Little Village ads, and the Douglas and Near West Side partners.
changes.why: They earn 0.8–1.6% each, and a party three days out leaves no time for word of mouth to spread.

e.note: A3 leads on every measure (19.2% reach, 10th percentile 17.1%, $624 per point, about 3x the benchmark's $1894) because early podcasts and the Nasty Gal drop give word of mouth time to work (58.6% of adoption), and even its 10th percentile beats A1's and A2's means. Late pop-ups (day 38), Little Village social ads and the Douglas and Near West Side partners return little for their cost, and McKinley Park (zone 2, fit 0.713) is barely seeded by A3.

e.text: Revising A3 per the Critic: add Elite Daily drop and cheap McKinley Park and Little Village partners.

e.note: Revising: Keep A3 podcasts early and Nasty Gal drop. Add Elite Daily drop funded by trimming Lower West Side social ads; add One City Tap, Mi Tierra, Co-Prosperity $300 partners. No late pop-ups, no Douglas/Near West Side. Variant 2: drop one podcast for both drops plus more partners.

e.note: Writing the launch plan for B2

plan.headline: Taste-matched Pilsen partners plus one podcast reach 20.8% of natural audience, 3.3x benchmark
plan.summary: The bet: keep Insanely Chill and the Nasty Gal drop as the early spark, then saturate Lower West Side, McKinley Park and Little Village with ten $300 partners and local ads so word of mouth carries the rest. Qloo taste data shows this crowd over-indexes heavily on Insanely Chill (0.96), Nasty Gal (0.95) and these venues (0.81–0.88), pulled in by Kali Uchis, Omar Apollo, Cuco and Rauw Alejandro. In simulation this reaches 20.8% of the natural audience (19.0%–23.4%) at $570 per point versus $1,894 for the benchmark, with word of mouth driving 58.6% of adoption; this is a model projection on Qloo taste data, not a guarantee.
